description: iTrust, the Centre for Research in Cyber Security at the Singapore University of Technology and Design, runs operational technology testbeds of critical infrastructure and releases the data collected on them to researchers worldwide free of charge. The testbeds are often run non-stop for several days with and without attacks. The datasets listed are Secure Water Treatment (SWaT), Water Distribution (WADI), Electric Power and Intelligent Control (EPIC), Internet of Things, the BATtle of Attack Detection Algorithms (BATADAL), Blaq_0 and data from the Critical Infrastructure Security Showdown (CISS), an annual operational technology cyber exercise open to red teams worldwide. Coverage: laboratory testbeds in Singapore. Format and access: data are provided on request through a form, processed within about three working days; the dataset characteristics page describes each set; free. Licence: iTrust terms of usage apply; data are given in good faith and as is, and since 1 July 2022 iTrust gives no follow-up support. Caveats: the data come from laboratory testbeds, not operating plants; data formats and sizes were not read. Simulation uses: training and testing attack detection and resilience of water treatment, water distribution and power control systems. Related records: the CIC datasets (data-cic-unb-cybersecurity-datasets) include a simulated substation network, and SANDI-2024 (data-sandi-2024-substation-intrusion-detection) is another substation set.
